Definition: a cloud (as covering the sky), i.e. the nimbus or thunder-cloud
BiblicalUsage: The cloud is God's covering through the whole Old Testament: the LORD went before Israel by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead them the way; the cloud covered the tent of the congregation and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle; the LORD came down in the pillar of the cloud and stood in the door of the tabernacle and called Aaron and Miriam; and when the priests came out of the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD. The cloud leads, the cloud covers, and the cloud is where God speaks.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cloud tells the truth about God: He is near enough to lead us and hidden enough that we cannot manage Him. He goes before His people in the cloud and He fills the house in the cloud, and I hold that is still how He works — present and guiding, and still beyond my full sight, which is why I trust what He has said rather than what I can see.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea; Building of Solomon's Temple
